CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports doing well. She has been taking prednisone 1 mg daily, which appears to be sufficient. She occasionally took an extra prednisone dose approximately once per week due to increased pain in her feet, particularly on days when she is more active despite having a desk job. Patient reports that methotrexate has definitely helped with her joint pain. She discontinued methotrexate for one week prior to receiving her first COVID vaccine due to concerns about potential interference with vaccine efficacy based on information received. She experienced significant pain during that week and resumed methotrexate one week later. For the second COVID vaccine dose, she was advised by a hotline to continue methotrexate and did so. Patient reports easy bruising that appears spontaneously without feeling the impact. She denies knowing the source of the bruises.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain in her feet joints and some pain in other joints. She notes that knee pain was present before methotrexate dose increase but has improved significantly since then. She reports ridges in her nails consistent with psoriasis, which have been present for a long time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily.
Methotrexate.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Feet examined with shoes and socks removed. Patient has pain in foot joints. Knee flexion elicited some discomfort. Good range of motion in toes. Ridges noted in nails consistent with psoriasis.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis on methotrexate with good response. Prednisone to be discontinued today. Patient to monitor for resolution of bruising as prednisone is tapered. Patient to schedule blood work appointment at front desk. Follow-up in three months.
